back: The area of land drained by a river and its tributaries, bounded by the watershed; an open system.

front: Inputs and outputs of a basin
back: Input: precipitation. Outputs: evapotranspiration (evaporation and transpiration) and channel flow to the sea.
Interception, surface storage, soil moisture, groundwater and channel storage.
Stemflow, throughfall, infiltration, overland flow, throughflow, percolation and groundwater flow.
The maximum rate at which the soil can absorb water; rain faster than this runs off as overland flow.
Groundwater contribution to a river, which sustains flow between storms and in the dry season.
P = Q + E ± ΔS (precipitation = runoff + evapotranspiration ± change in storage), all in mm.
Circular basin: short lag, high sharp peak. Elongated basin: longer lag, lower peak.

front: Effects of urbanisation on the basin
back: Impermeable surfaces and drains reduce infiltration and speed up runoff, so peaks are higher and baseflow is lower.
